summary: Wayfarers of the South Tigris has players sending caravans of worker-dice out from Baghdad to explore land, water, and sky tiles, racing to fill in a shared modular map before returning home to report findings. It's a mid-weight exploration and set-collection game with light worker-placement-with-dice-workers mechanics, played mostly on your own tableau with the occasional bump into rivals over map tiles.
praised: attractive, tactile modular map that grows during play
smooth engine with satisfying tableau development
good mix of planning and light tactics without excessive downtime
criticised: can feel somewhat solitaire/parallel with limited direct interaction
some rules overhead for a mid-weight game
map tile luck can favor some players
mechanically similar to the designers' other games, so less novel for series fans

interaction.kind: competing for limited worker-placement action spots and area majority on shared modular map tiles
interaction.detail: Players place dice-workers on a shared action board where spots can be taken before you get to them, and they compete for area-majority control on the modular exploration tiles. Still, a large portion of each turn is spent advancing your own caravan and journal track independent of what others do.
interaction.said: unknown — Garphill/Shem Phillips games are generally noted for being fairly parallel with some competitive edge over shared worker spots and map tiles rather than being described as mean or cutthroat

scoring.how_you_win: You spend the game mapping land, water, and sky tiles into sets, upgrading your caravan, and building influence with the three guilds; once a player reaches the final column of the Journal track everyone else gets one last turn, then all these sources are tallied and the highest total wins.
